cover.headline:
A workspace that stays
secure and clear as you grow.
cover.lede: A two-week audit of The Merrittocracy's Notion workspace, ending in a report of quick wins and prioritised recommendations. Based on our conversation on November 13.

glance.p: Structure, access and navigation come first.
Do it yourselves, with AI, or with us.

context.title:
What we
heard.
context.lede: The Merrittocracy is a social justice agency that brings strategy, research, creative work and implementation together. The team runs its core systems in Notion, with important files linked to Google Drive and Claude helping with meeting minutes and incoming emails. As the team grows, you want the workspace to stay secure, efficient and easy to navigate.

stats.t: people on the team, and growing
core systems in Notion: programmes, CRM, finances, capacity and information

context.pains_title: Three things to sort out before the team grows.

pains.p: Access is decided page by page. That gets harder to keep secure with every new person, especially around sensitive data.
Graphs, projects and several views on one page take time to load and are hard for a new team member to read.

pains.h: Updates that are hard to find
pains.it: "Is there anything on the Business plan that we should be using that we're not?"
pains.p: Claude's project updates land as comments, which get harder to find as they pile up. Meeting notes live in Gemini, outside the workspace.

quote.text: We've got everything we need. We just need to make it much more efficiently structured.

context.opportunity: You already have the core systems and the information in place. Before adding more processes, an audit shows how to make what you have clearer, more secure and easier for a growing team to use, without over-engineering the workspace.

proposal.title:
One audit,
one clear price.
proposal.intro: We review how the workspace is built and how the team uses it, then hand you a report you can act on. Implementation is a separate, optional step that we scope together once you have read the report.

phases.name: Workspace audit and report
phases.summary: We meet with you and the team, review the workspace from the inside and deliver a written report.
deliverables: Two sessions with Marcus and the team to understand how the workspace is used
Review of structure, databases, teamspaces, permissions and dashboard navigation
Assessment of your Claude, Google Drive and meeting-note workflows
Audit report with quick wins and prioritised recommendations, marking what the team can do itself, where AI can help and where our support would be useful
